[b]DAESUN SEIZES VALDDERAN ISLANDS[/b]

[i]After hours of brutal fighting the Daesunite Ministry of Defence is proud to announce the capture of the Northern and Southern Valdderan archipelago. All Valdderan military contest has completely annihilated and the islands are pacified. The islands have been designated with codenames operating by Occupied Security Zones(OSZ's), with their names being OSZ-1, OSZ-2, OSZ-3, OSZ-4, and OSZ-5. Daesun seeks to integrate and incorporate these islands into the United Daesunite Federation (UDF), justifying action via historical claims, large Daesunite population, economic, and political ties to the islands. While strategically valuable, the islands are still too unpopulated for statehood, and therefore will be designated as overseas territories until they reach suffice-able population.

Daesun also looks towards beginning the Jorge initiative, an economic revitalization plan fixed on restoring the resource industries of the islands. Daesun seeks to flood the islands with government subsidies to companies willing to invest into their development. Companies who are able to develop assets within the islands the most will recieve highest incentive, creating a perfect environment for competition and rapid growth. 

But Daesun wouldn't seek to seize the islands without the word of the people, as that went against every core value that she held dearly. A series of referendums were held all across each OSZs, each to be free and fair without the use of fear or intimidation. The referendum's prompt was simple, "Do you wish for your OSZ to join the Daesunite Federation?", yet it sent shockwaves. Daesun secured a desisive victory in all OSZs, primarily due to civil discontent with the Valdderan government's expensive and bloody intervention into Tirakan. The results of the referendums were as follows...

OSZ-1: 64.3% Aye, 28.9% Nay, 6.8% Neutral

OSZ-2: 86.4% Aye, 11.2% Nay, 2.4% Neutral

OSZ-3: 91.5% Aye, 4.2% Nay, 4.3% Neutral

OSZ-4: 54.2% Aye, 41.7% Nay, 4.1% Neutral

OSZ-5: 77.2% Aye, 22.1% Nay 0.7% Neutral

With the referendums done, each territory would be processed for incorporation, with actual territory-hood estimated to begin in mid 2027.

[b]On Maarav Self-Determination: By Hashban Ben Yegad, supreme Shofet of the Bene HaMaarav[/b]

In the recent days we have seen many opinions be released on the matter of the Autonomous Socialist Republic of Maarav. Indeed many view the ASRM as some sort of puppet regime placed upon us by some colonialist power. 

However, if one was to visit the territory of Maarav prior to the formation of the ASRM they would see something far from colonialism. The torah commands of us as faithful Israelites to love the foreigner as a citizen of our own state, thus we have done this in accordance with the Holy law of Hashem. 

The Thrømm came and did not oppress us, though they couldve chosen to, they merely set up their army to protect us who pleaded to Elohim for aid against our enemies, from the greater threat of the Sal-Baliz, our autonomous jurisdiction was always guaranteed, our religion unimpeded. In return we have aided and joined with the Thrømm in their fight and see them not as foreigners but the righteous among the nations, those from afar who were promised to be brought near by the prophets. 

It is my hope that this may provide clarity on our situation.


[spoiler=[b][u]Shahid Salama - The Islamic Socialist Republic of Sabrata - Late 1953[/u][/b]]

[b][i]September[/i][/b]

[i]A line there, another just to the side of it. Slow movement is key to precision, and the decorative architecture takes time to replicate, even if it was relatively simple. And that's this side done. Now to start on the 4th side tomorrow. Putting his drawing book and pencil back in his shoulder bag, he stands up from the shaded spot he has been for half of the afternoon now. Someone runs past, towards the town square. In the distance, a large plume of dust grows in the air, signaling something is coming to the town. A vehicle no doubt, most likely a farmer coming back from the market.

A calm stroll could help him clear his mind before dinner, especially now that the heat is making way for winter. Maybe hell go look at the nature which grows by the river. That would be nice. 
Before he can go for his stroll, someone grabs him and turns him around. Its his mother, looking frightened and scared. [/i]Shahid. You need to come home. [i]Before he can even answer or ask what is going on, his mother grabs his hand and pulls him, almost making him fall onto the ground before he could get his legs moving. [/i]

[i]Weaving through roads and alleyways, they finally get home. His mother is frantic, closing shutters on their windows and doing anything to make the house as closed off as possible. [/i]Mother, what's happening? What's wrong? [i]He rests a hand on her shoulder, finally getting her to stop the panic which has gripped his mothers mind. She answers in an exasperated voice. [/i]They are here for you, for you all. [i]Given only these words, his mother goes back to checking every window. Before he can check the mental state of his mother once again, a loud, hard banging is heard from the door.[/i] 

Go. Go to your room and hide. [i]His mother pushes him towards his room before waiting for him to comply. Doing so, he catches a glimpse of his mother heading to answer the door. Now in his room, he must find somewhere to conceal himself. No good options are present, but as he considers his options, the sound of a cup shattering against his door breaks his train of thought. Shouting can be heard from the main room, and it souls like a man. [/i]Where is he? [i]Yet another item is thrown somewhere and breaks against a wall. [/i]We know you have a son! Tell us where he is now! [i]His mother cries out, desperate. [/i]I dont know! He isnt home! 

[i]He must intervene now, before it gets any worse. Exiting his room, he gets a full view of the scene. Two men, one with a pistol and one with a rifle are standing around his mother, interrogating her, both dressed like soldiers in tan uniforms. He must reveal himself [/i]Im right here. Im here. [i]He walks into the center of the room, his hands in the air. He does his best to not look scared, facing the armed men. The man with the pistol would address him. [/i]Pack your things. The General has decided more men must be prepared to push the western king out of our land. Meet us in the town square in a half hour or your family will be punished.

[i]After they leave, his mother turns to him. [/i]Please my son, dont go. I cant have you go. [i]Shahid did his best to look his mother in the eyes and not be scared. To be strong and console her,  but every second which he stared at his mothers desperate face, that facade was failing. [/i]I must mother, I must keep you safe. Father will help you understand once he is back, he would agree I should go.[i] Now he must pack his things. First would be a blanket, next would be some preserved foods, and finally would be a change of clothes if he ever needed them. He would leave the house now, but he couldnt leave his mother like this. Giving her one final embrace, he would assure her. [/i]Im only 15, they will just have me managing supplies. Ill come back, okay? [i]With his mother giving a reluctant nod, he would head for the town square.[/i]

[i]In the town center, two other soldiers stood guard of a CADT truck, its old royal army insignias still visible despite the attempts of the revolutionaries to remove them. It seems they either dont care to repaint them or just dont have enough for all the vehicles. Walking up to the guards, one brought him to the back of the truck where he was instructed to climb inside the canvas covered bed. He hesitated a little until the soldier began to move his hands on his rifle to a position better for bashing him with the buttstock. Quickly clambering into the covered truckbed, he came face to face with almost 20 other kids his age, all with their own small collections of possessions. Not taking the time to see if he recognized any of them, he took one of the few open spots on the trucks bench. From next to him, he heard a whisper. [/i]Is that you Shahid? [i]He recognized that voice well, after all he heard it everyday since he could remember. [/i]Yes, its me Zahir. Good to see Im not the only one, [i]he whispered back.[/i]

[i]It was only a couple dozen minutes before the last of the sons were in the back of the truck, 22 in total. A few unlucky ones had to sit on the bed of the truck when the two guards got in the back as well, however the bench didnt offer much comfort over the truckbed anyway. The two who had visited Shahids house got in the cab of the truck and they were off. First out of the square, then the village, then on the way to wherever they were being taken. The ride remained somewhat interesting with Zahir and the others providing a source of entertainment via conversation and theories on where they were going and what they would do once under the command of the General. One said he was related to Nidal Younis and would fly fighter planes, doing rolls and aerobatics like his supposed uncle. Two others said they would become tankers together, being invincible while rolling over enemy positions. Sometimes the guards would smile a little when a kid mentioned a certain thing, but they mostly talked to each other or just stared at the passing scenery.

They drove into the late afternoon and evening, only stopping when the slighted eek of light was still illuminating the landscape. Most were asleep, using each other's shoulders as pillows for the ones on the benches and the ones on the floor just using their packs. Shahid however couldnt sleep. He was too worried about his mother, and what would happen to him and the others. He heard the truck come to a stop, the driver and another man in the cab talking with someone, who from what he could hear, was a gate guard for some camp. This must be where they will be trained. The conversation ended as the sound of metal hinges signaled they were being let in. Accelerating forward, through the gate, they were finally in Camp Abd al-Fattah.

One by one, the boys would nudge each other awake, barely getting all of them lucid in time to meet the wrath of one of the camps instructors. They quickly disembarked from the truck, being led by the two guards and the instructor to a single story concrete barracks, which inside were 16 somewhat run down metal bunkbeds, eight for each side. They were gathered into a formation of two columns, 11 per line, and the instructor began talking.[/i] This barracks will be your home for the next three weeks! I expect it to be well taken care of during that time! Training starts at 0500 tomorrow! [i]Nobody moved a muscle until the instructor and the guards left, but the second they did, it was like they were children again. Peers raced each other to get the top bunks, and some explored the building looking for every interesting and unknown thing they could find. Shahid would lose his race with Zahir for the top bunk, being relegated to the lower bunk. Most, including Shahid, would be asleep when the rest of the barracks arrived, the instructors yelling waking them up with a shock. After the instructor and guards left yet again, the group from their village and the new group would become acquainted. A few stories would be exchanged and a few would make new friends before the mandatory lights out, sending even the most excited ones to sleep. 

The next three weeks would be a blur of learning, exhaustion, and speculation. Their first bugle call would come much too early for what they were used to, the second wake up call being the instructor from the last night barging in and yelling at those still in bed. While it was still dark, they would be marched to the medical building, where they revived examinations. After each examination they each walked to a guard at the end of the hall, who gave them two pairs of basic uniforms and one pair of boots. Many who got these uniforms didnt have matching sizes of clothing at all, and needed to trade to others for correct sizes. Those who didnt manage to trade had to roll up sleeves and pant legs as well as fashion belts out of the one pair of extra long shoelaces they were handed along with the boots. Few noticed at the time, but most of the uniforms were slightly discolored in places where holes were patched up. 

After they were changed, they marched back to the barracks to drop off their extra and old clothes, then to the canteen. At the mess hall, they were served a bowl of Sharba (lamb soup) and bread. They were told to eat fast, and they did, nobody daring to stop and savor the flavor of the admittedly somehow bland soup. The cooking here was definitely not up to the standard they were used to, but it wasnt bad. At least it was served hot. After about 15 minutes, they were marched to the main training area. A different instructor than they were used to explained the rules of the camp and training. Do not disobey your instructor, do not leave the camp unless specifically ordered to and with a guard present, etc. After the rules were explained, the training jumpstarted. This day was physical training. They climbed ropes, did pullups, pushups, attempted the obstacle course, and ran, only taking breaks for lunch and dinner, plus marching between areas. At the end of the day, each changed into just a pair of shorts and a shirt before falling asleep instantly.

Day after day, they did the same as the last with only what they were learning changing, and sometimes the food. They began learning how to handle and service firearms, navigate terrain, and medical skills, all while the guards and instructors noted down the most promising in each field. A few accidents happened, chief among them being during rifle training. One of them has been using their rifle to lean on at some time between receiving it and going up to shoot, resulting in some dirt being stuck in the barrel. When he went to shoot, the barrel exploded and hit the kid next to him with a small amount of shrapnel. That guy was chewed out bad for that one and got kitchen duty for almost the remainder of training. Another time came when they were training with grenades. They mostly trained with ones which had the explosive bits taken out, but they each threw one real one at the end of training. This occasion came a day after a rare rain hit the camp, making almost everything muddy  and the sun hadnt had enough time to dry everything out yet. One kid who was throwing his grenade slipped, resulting in it falling into the mud right next to where he was standing. Thankfully, the instructor tackled him into a ditch which was nearby made exactly for this. Both ended up safe, but came up with their uniforms more brown than tan.

The instructors were mean, but one of them dished out a few less punishments than the rest. This merciful instructor was the primary medical instructor, Instructor Wali. While he still did dish out harsh punishments for infractions like the others, he handled them making mistakes much better. Once Shahid forgot an important part of the instructional medical kit which they practiced with, and Instructor Wali asked him what he was missing. After quickly scanning his kit, he answered [/i]My disinfectant? Yes. [i]Wali would chime back. [/i]And what is its full name? [i]Shahid would take a few moments to rack his brain before responding. [/i]Sulfanilamide? [i]Wali smiled.[/i] Good. Now go grab it and we will start. [i]This disinfectant was really just a fake powder meant to imitate the powder. Wali was also the person who oversaw the medical examinations as well as chose the people who would be selected to become medics. Many treated his instructional time as a relief from the rest of the day.

Finally, the three weeks were up for their group. At a ceremony, they were lined up and each received their assignment from the camps political officer. Most were assigned to what was called forward assault infantry, and some who Instructor Wali saw promise in became medical assistants to actual battlefield medics. Some boys from the other batch who joined them on the first day were assigned to vehicle training as they had experience driving trucks. The most surprising of all though was the one with the ace as his supposed uncle, who was assigned to aircraft training, which was a bit unspecific. Maybe he was telling the truth. After the ceremony, they all went back to the barracks to pack their things for tomorrow. The only exception were the ones who were selected to be medical assistants, as they were kept behind for a few days so they could be trained how to do a more thorough medical examination. That's probably why those medical examiners they went to on the first day looked so young.

Most were restless throughout the night just like the first day of training, but this time they were used to the schedule. In the morning, they cleaned their uniforms and lined up next to the exact same gate they entered just three weeks earlier as the kids their parents knew. Now they were soldiers. Those selected for the forward assault infantry would be shipped out of camp first, two trucks waiting for them next to the gate. Loading into the trucks, they held themselves high. Each was giddy with excitement, but uncertainty lurked in the back of Shahids mind. The questions of his fate were slowly replaced by the tiredness overcoming him. He would have time to worry when he got to wherever they were going.
[/i] [/spoiler]
